change: New complete groups only. V15 prompt, model, effort, runner and serialization unchanged.
prompt_template:
Write the most precise and concise category title for the subject matter supported by every instance.

Interpret the quoted text within each instance together.

For each instance, ask yourself: "Given this instance alone, must its subject matter belong to the category named by this title?"

Instances:

{NUMBERED_INSTANCES}

groups.selection_rationale: Several related opinions and processes expressed through separated fragments; shared subject must remain useful without copying every detail.
Short expressions with an implicit ordinary subject and different attitudes toward it; keep limited evidence intact.
Mostly greetings with morning-coffee and afternoon instances; test an entire heterogeneous group rather than trimming difficult members.
Two distinct foods sharing an explicit cuisine context; avoid replacing subject meaning with a list of word types.
Technical and sensory descriptions about meat; test ordinary semantic interpretation without importing source-note context.
Hashtag-only fragments alongside a sipping fragment; test naming subject matter despite marker-like input.

question: Does unchanged v15 produce useful, concise subject-category titles for a small diverse selection of previously unused complete HDBv2 groups?
evaluation: Interpret each mask's exact fragments together with ordinary semantic knowledge; judge the named subject against all members.
Do not demand one canonical title or literal word overlap. A title can cover alternatives and broader wording can be acceptable.
Do not name the text's formatting instead of its subject. Advice and other textual subjects remain valid when they are the actual subject matter.

The user accepted Brisket smoking for the preceding group containing a bare brisket mask and smoking masks. Preserve that case-specific decision rather than treating it as an outstanding failure or silently inferring a new universal rule.
Separate a weak source mask or a heterogeneous grouping from a title-generation error; do not repair inputs or invent specificity to force a pass.
Preserve all responses, explicitly distinguish assistant uncertainty from clear errors, and record no user decisions automatically.

selection.limitation: New group memberships from the same 100-note food-centered corpus, not new source notes by definition, an independent corpus or a general accuracy estimate.

comparison: Two repetitions of unchanged v15. No same-group prior title baseline; the review comparison shows the other trial. This selected sample is not a population estimate.
execution: One new isolated subscription-authenticated Codex process/thread/empty workspace per group and trial. Same pinned CLI and wrapper as v15; no extra schema, tools, web, examples, expected titles, full source notes or review comments supplied. Three concurrent calls at most; no retry or best-of.
budget: Existing subscription allowance only. No new API billing, rental, purchase, credential changes or local model inference.
